subject_line: Yamuna, her mother and the house in Chengalpattu
email_body:
Beste Jaco,

'n Goeie dag vir boomklim bly by my – Marnus wat moeg is om onsigbaar te wees tussen sy twee broers, en saam met Leila in die boom kamp sodat dit nie vir 'n pyplyn afgekap word nie. Dat die boek via die In Other Words-kompetisie in Engels verskyn het en op die Carnegie-langlys beland het, is 'n merkwaardige reis.

Skryf jy anders vir Afrikaanse lesers noudat jou boeke ook in vertaling gelees word?

The Author Ledger is 'n onafhanklike projek met kort Author Spotlights. Die portret word deur 'n paar geskrewe vrae opgebou wat jy op jou eie tyd kan beantwoord, en die volledige teks word vir jou hersiening gestuur voordat dit gepubliseer word.

Sou jy belangstel om deel te neem?

Vriendelike groete
The Author Ledger

subject_line: Why Cape Fever could only be set in Cape Town
email_body:
Dear Nadia,

In a podcast conversation about Cape Fever you spoke about your long relationship with Cape Town and why the novel could not have been set anywhere else. A 1920s gothic told through a young maid caught up with the spirits of a decaying manor feels like a real turn after An Imperfect Blessing and your Caine Prize-winning story "Bridling".

For a Spotlight, I would love to ask what the gothic form allowed you to say about the city that realism did not.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. The portrait is developed through a few written questions, which you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part?

Best regards,
The Author Ledger

subject_line: Three names, one writer: from The Law of Tall Girls to Jo Macgregor
email_body:
Dear Joanne,

What caught my attention is how your work is split across three names: young adult fiction such as The Law of Tall Girls under Joanne Macgregor, adult crime as Jo Macgregor, and self-help as J. Macgregor, adding up to seventeen books across genres. I also noticed you on the 2025 Knysna Literary Festival line-up.

For a Spotlight, I would like to ask how you decide which name a new idea belongs to, and whether the voices ever leak into one another.

subject_line: Writing Molo: The Last Villains of Molo and Den of Inequities
email_body:
Dear Kinyanjui,

The Last Villains of Molo takes its title from the place you were born, and I was struck that it and Den of Inequities have been taught at undergraduate and postgraduate level. It is not a usual path for a novelist who has also built a career in banking.

For a Spotlight, I would like to ask how the two working lives sit together, and what it is like to see a novel rooted in Molo read in lecture halls.

subject_line: Mombasa roots and Let's Talk About This
email_body:
Dear Moraa,

I came across your young adult novels, from Let's Talk About This and The Kigango Oracle to Hila and The Shark Attack, and noted that you were born in Mombasa. Titles like these suggest a writer who takes teenage readers' questions seriously and is happy to move between frank conversation and adventure.

For a Spotlight, I would like to ask how the coast shaped your sense of story, and what young Kenyan readers tell you they want from a book.
